records.title: CIPP Future of Payroll Research Report 2020
records.fieldwork_period: Survey distributed approximately eight weeks into the UK lockdown starting 23 March 2020; precise dates not established
records.population: UK payroll professionals, including employer and service-provider perspectives
records.funding: Report names JGA, Workday and Zellis as supporters/sponsors
records.review_status: Original hosted report text reviewed; selected item bases in Nick Day foreword; final graphic checks not performed

claims.finding: JGA is named among sponsors; Nick Day is named Managing director in the JGA foreword.
claims.use: Research lineage; do not imply report ownership.

claims.finding: The foreword discusses future analytical, advisory, leadership and data skills alongside transactional automation.
claims.use: Attributed historical commentary, not proof subsequent outcomes occurred.

records.reuse_status: Private research retention only; publication reproduction and redistribution rights not established

records.title: CIPP Future of Payroll Report 2022
records.fieldwork_period: Survey posted online for one month; exact dates not established
records.population: UK payroll professionals, in-house and service-provider context
records.funding: Report names Datagraphic, Experian, JGA and Workday among supporters/sponsors
records.review_status: Original hosted report text reviewed; no final claim-specific graphic check

claims.finding: Nick Day is named Managing director of JGA Recruitment Group and contributes a foreword about education, skills and payroll transformation.
claims.use: Direct brand-specific history; distinguish foreword expectations from survey findings.

claims.finding: The report covers strategic value, future payments, education and technology.
claims.use: Challenge any broad topic novelty claim.

records.title: CIPP Future of Payroll Report 2024
records.population: Mixed UK payroll professionals in-house and provider teams across industries
records.review_status: Original hosted text reviewed; achieved sample described only as hundreds in the inspected foreword; item-specific bases unavailable

claims.locator: Printed p4 AI benefits and considerations
claims.finding: Separate reported measures include AI use 6%, RPA use17%, and 48% unable to distinguish AI from RPA.
claims.use: Context for task-level clarification; not comparable adoption measures across studies.

claims.finding: 53% chose the response combining no current change with happiness with current software.
claims.use: Counterevidence to universal dissatisfaction; do not infer UK employer prevalence.

records.title: 2025 Getting the World Paid Survey Report
records.population: Global payroll professionals; most respondents US-located; mixed manager/specialist/analyst roles
records.funding: Publisher is a professional payroll body; report acknowledgements require final funding/rights review
records.review_status: Original PDF text reviewed; full appendix contains item-specific response bases, not extracted for selected qualitative context

claims.finding: Method describes585 respondents and collection dates, with most respondents located in the US.
claims.use: Population context, not JGA UK prevalence.

claims.finding: The report identifies source/input data and cut-off issues among accuracy challenges despite connected technology.
claims.use: Probe cross-functional handoffs; reported causes are not independently proven causal mechanisms.
